name: Football Scoreboard
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Standalone plugin for live, recent, and upcoming football games across NFL and NCAA Football with real-time scores, down/distance, possession, and game status. Now with organized nested config!

versions.notes: Three timing and selection fixes measured on a live board. (1) A mode retaking the panel now gives its current card a full turn: the dwell clock kept running while the mode was off screen, so the first display() call after every block advanced immediately -- the card cut off by the previous block's end was skipped instead of shown (one in five card transitions on a 30s block of 15s cards), and after a service restart the clock started at manager construction, producing a 9s card and a 5s card in the first block. (2) schedule_lookahead_days is now enforced at selection, not just in the ranged fetch: selection reads the season-wide background cache, so every published fixture was eligible and a board with no NFL football inside its 7-day window filled with games four weeks out, exactly what the config's own description says cannot happen. (3) The favourite-check advisory now reports the first game's date instead of a league-calendar week boundary, which routinely opens days before its first game -- it claimed 'nothing on until 06 September' for a league whose first snap is the 10th.
versions.changelog: A mode retaking the panel gives its current card a full turn instead of instantly advancing past the card the previous block cut off; the first cards after a service restart get their full duration too. schedule_lookahead_days is enforced at selection, so fixtures beyond the horizon no longer reach the board through the season-wide cache. The 'nothing on until' advisory reports the first game's date, not a calendar week boundary.

versions.notes: Recent games now get their odds too. SportsUpcoming fetches odds for the games that survive selection and SportsLive fetches them per included game -- the Recent screen never fetched them at all. A final only showed a line when the other-games rotation happened to swap it in (2.29.2 fetches odds for each fresh slice), and a league whose recent pool fits inside its limits never rotates: its finals stayed bare while a busier league's rotated cards drew theirs. Observed live with both leagues' show_odds on: NFL's eight recents rotated and showed closing lines, NCAA's lone final never did. Recent's update() now fetches odds for the selected finals, exactly as Upcoming does; ESPN keeps a completed game's closing line on the same endpoint, so a final is as answerable as an upcoming game.
versions.changelog: Recent games now get their odds too. The Recent screen never fetched odds itself -- a final only showed a line when the rotation happened to swap it in, so a league whose recent pool fits inside its limits (no rotation) showed bare finals while a busier league's rotated cards drew theirs. Recent's update() now fetches odds for the selected finals, exactly as Upcoming does.

versions.notes: Rotated-in games now get their odds. Odds are fetched in update(), which for an upcoming list runs hourly, while the other-games rotation re-cuts the non-favourite slice every other_rotation_interval_seconds on the display path -- deliberately with no network work. Every slice cut between updates therefore rendered without a line even though ESPN had one, while the favourites, which survive every cut, kept the odds update() gave them. The rotation now hands the freshly swapped-in games to a background thread that asks the odds manager about each one -- bounded by the slice, never the pool, so a college league's hundreds of upcoming games are still never trawled -- and a line appears on the card as soon as its fetch lands. Cached per game, so a game re-entering the window inside the odds TTL costs a lookup rather than a request.
versions.changelog: Rotated-in games now get their odds. The other-games rotation re-cuts the slice on the display path between hourly updates, and only update() fetched odds -- so rotated-in cards rendered without a line even though ESPN had one, while favourites kept theirs. The rotation now hands the fresh slice to a background thread, bounded by the slice size, with per-game caching.

versions.notes: The full-screen upcoming scoreboard draws its date and time again on configs that had hidden them on the scroll card. Show Date and Show Time predate the full-screen display reading the scroll_card block: they governed only the scroll and Vegas cards, so turning them off there never touched the stacked date and time in the middle of the switch-mode scorebug -- until the block was wired through, when those old settings started silently blanking it. The full-screen display now has its own switch_show_date and switch_show_time, both defaulting to true, holding it to what it has always drawn -- the same back-compat rule that gave it switch_upcoming_center and switch_date_format. The scroll and Vegas cards keep following Show Date and Show Time exactly as before.
versions.changelog: The full-screen upcoming scoreboard draws its date and time again on configs that had hidden them on the scroll card. Show Date and Show Time governed only the scroll and Vegas cards before the full-screen display read the scroll_card block, so those old settings had started silently blanking a scorebug that has always drawn both lines. It now has its own switch_show_date and switch_show_time, both defaulting to true; the scroll and Vegas cards keep following Show Date and Show Time exactly as before.

versions.notes: The score is now the headline it was always meant to be. It was the only element on the card not sized from the panel, and it was not even bigger than its neighbours: PressStart2P renders crisply on an 8px grid, so the 10px default snapped to 8 -- the same 8 the clock above it and the game date below it are drawn at. It is now sized from display_height, snapped to its face's pixel grid and capped at twice its design size, with the clock/date face held a grid step below it. Score and date positions scale with their faces so a grown one is not clipped off the card. Where the grown score would swamp the panel the layout now reaches for a narrower FACE rather than crowding out the logos, which is what football-scoreboard has always done and the single reason its logos read larger than every other scoreboard's at the same size. Measured on a 128x64 board: 4x6-font at 14px reserves 28px and leaves 52x52 logos, where PressStart2P at 16px reserved 60px and left 36x36 -- two small badges adrift in a mostly black panel. The two faces are nothing like the same shape: PressStart2P is square, 4x6-font is nearly as tall and about half as wide, so the score keeps the dimension that carries legibility and gives back the one the logos need. Logos are sized against the space the score actually needs, and only where the score grew -- a panel whose score did not move keeps exactly the logos it had. The upcoming screen is untouched at every size: it draws no score, so none of this applies to it -- its date and time keep the face and size they always had. Measured on the live and recent screens: 64x32, 128x32 and 256x32 render byte-identically to the previous release, and every taller panel gains a larger score with logos the score is no longer drawn across. The adaptive layout reaches the same rung: fit_text_proportional takes the largest rung at or below its target, and 8 * (48/32) = 12 fell just short of 16, so a 48-tall card got the same 8px score a 32-tall one did. _fit_element now snaps the score's target to the face's grid first, so both layouts pick the same size on the same panel. The snap is opt-in per call rather than keyed on the font name, because the score font also draws the "VS" separator and the stacked date/time on an upcoming card: those are not scores and keep the size they always had.

versions.notes: The text colour pickers in Customization now actually colour the text. score_text, period_text, team_name, status_text, detail_text and rank_text have each offered a colour in the web UI for as long as they have had a font, and setting one changed only which font was loaded -- every string was drawn white. The colour now follows the face it belongs to, on the full-screen scoreboard and on the scroll and Vegas cards alike. Every default is white, so a display nobody has recoloured looks exactly as it did. The adaptive layout honours the same colours by the same rule: the clock, a recent card's Final and the kickoff time take period_text's colour, the stacked centre takes score_text's, the bottom date line takes detail_text's; records, timeouts and the semantic fills keep their own.

The colour now follows the face it belongs to, on the full-screen scoreboard and on the scroll and Vegas cards alike. versions.notes: Fix a crash when the date format is set to "weekday". game_renderer.py used datetime, timezone and ZoneInfo without importing any of them, so choosing that option -- one of the documented values of scroll_card.date_format -- raised NameError. Neither helper's except clause catches NameError (_weekday_for catches ValueError/TypeError, _card_tzinfo catches KeyError/ValueError/TypeError/OSError), so it propagated out of the render rather than falling back to the plain date. The imports now match hockey-scoreboard, the one copy that always had them and rendered the option correctly. Nothing else changes: the default "abbrev" format, which is what the render harness and the golden images exercise, was never affected, which is how this went unnoticed.

Keep the possession football on the panel and clear of everything else, and stop the adaptive layout dropping the yardage. The ball was placed a fixed 3px from the down and distance text and guarded only by a check that its x had not come out negative -- which tests that a number was not negative, not that the ball fit anywhere. On a 64px-wide panel it landed on the timeout bars; on the adaptive 256x128 card it was drawn at x 262-274 of a 256px card, entirely off the edge. Its size and the wording beside it are unchanged: the ball is placed around the text now, never the other way round, and where a row genuinely cannot hold both -- a 64x32 leaves about 30px between the timeout bars and the text alone wants 29 -- the down and distance wins and the ball is omitted. Separately, the adaptive card drew the down and distance in PressStart2P, roughly four times wider per character than the 4x6 face: on a 192x48 panel that rendered "3rd & 8 at KC 42" 128px wide against the classic layout's 65px, and on a 256x128 it reached the full 256px so the line was clipped at both ends. That line alone now uses the compact 4x6 face, verified crisp at both rungs; the clock, status band, records and dates keep the face and sizes they had. With the narrower face the yardage also fits where it previously did not -- the long form was gated on `display_width > 128`, a proxy for "is there room" that got a 128x64 wrong -- so it is now preferred whenever it fits the space the timeout bars and records leave free.

The new favourite-selection settings now reach the display: they were declared in the config form and read by the display code, but dropped in the translation between the two, so changing them did nothing. Other games are filtered by quality before they fill the remaining slots -- ranked teams by default -- and that now includes a board with no favourite teams at all, where every game shown is a non-favourite game and the setting previously did nothing. Favourites are never filtered. The FBS/FCS filter is limited to college football, the one league ESPN publishes those rosters for; elsewhere it no longer costs a lookup. College rankings are fetched from the endpoint that actually carries them, so the rank badge and the ranked filter work at all; each poll is fetched once rather than once per configured group; leagues with no poll no longer ask for one; and the division lookup expires instead of being held for the life of the process. Each plugin's README now documents how the selection settings actually behave. Both filters also fail open as a set: if they leave nothing to show at all -- no favourite playing and every other game rejected -- the unfiltered list is used rather than blanking the mode, and 'broadcast' allows everything in a league ESPN publishes no TV listings for. A poll that loads but matches no game on the schedule now says so in the log instead of quietly emptying the slots. The non-favourite slice now rotates on the display path rather than only when the game list is refetched, so other_rotation_interval_seconds finally means what it says -- it was gated behind an hourly update that nothing could change. Three settings the code reads are now reachable too: recent_update_interval, upcoming_update_interval and stale_game_timeout were stuck at their built-in defaults, and in three plugins the first two were shown in the config form while the translation dropped them. College football now defaults to five games rather than one, with no favorite team set: with no favorites configured every card is a non-favorite card, so one game meant one card repeating until the schedule moved on. Within the other-games pool the better matchup now leads: the slice is ordered by the best poll position of either side, so the top game of the week sits in the first window rather than whichever kicks off soonest. Favourites stay in kickoff order. Each team appears once in that pool -- its next game -- because the upcoming list is a whole season, not a week, and ranking it without that put the top team's entire schedule ahead of everyone else's opener. Favourite slots are shared between your teams: each gets its next game before any team gets a second, so a team on a bye is no longer crowded out by one that plays twice. Also fixed in this release: the rotation due-check now mirrors the composer's pool rule, so a board whose filters reject every other game while a favourite is playing no longer re-runs selection on every frame.

versions.notes: The matchup separator and the date and time formats now reach the full-screen scoreboard, not just the scroll and Vegas cards. A new "Middle of a Full-Screen Upcoming Scoreboard" setting (switch_upcoming_center) picks what sits between the two logos before a game starts: the stacked date and time as before, the VS / @ / at separator, nothing, or whatever the scroll and Vegas cards are set to. It defaults to the stacked date and time, so the scoreboard looks exactly as it did until you change it.

versions.notes: Fetch a team's badge when it is not already on disk. The shipped logo set covers FBS only, so an FCS opponent -- Furman, Tennessee State -- had no file and its card drew without logos. Nothing was logged and nothing errored, because nothing had failed: the file simply was not there. The request is now made where the game dict is built, using the logo URL ESPN returns in the same payload as the game, and the download runs on a small shared pool rather than inline -- a request is allowed 30s, so a game with two missing badges could otherwise hold its own detail extraction for a minute and delay every scoreboard update behind it. The pool's record of what is in flight and what could not be fetched is shared across the live, recent and upcoming managers and namespaced by sport, so the same badge is not queued three times. On a live rig this pulled 96 missing badges, taking the local set from 209 to 307.

Favorite teams now appear in upcoming and recent even when 'show favorite teams only' is off. New other_upcoming_games_to_show / other_recent_games_to_show control how many other games fill the rest, and other_rotation_interval_seconds advances that slice over time so the board works through the schedule instead of repeating the same handful.
versions.changelog: Favorite teams now appear in upcoming and recent even when 'show favorite teams only' is off. New other_upcoming_games_to_show / other_recent_games_to_show control how many other games fill the rest, and other_rotation_interval_seconds advances that slice over time so the board works through the schedule instead of repeating the same handful.

versions.notes: Stop the scorebug overprinting itself on small panels. Logos were sized at 1.5x the panel so they bleed off the outer edge, which is fine when the panel is wide; at 64x32 it made each logo 48px at x=-10 and x=26, so the two logos overlapped each other across the middle before the score or clock were drawn. They are now capped so the pair always leaves the centre clear for the score, which binds only where the 1.5x did not fit -- 128x32 and 512x64 keep the logo sizes they had. Status and down-and-distance also shed detail rather than overflowing: Q4 02:34 is 64px at 8px, the entire width of a 64px panel, so it spanned edge to edge with its outline clipped and collided with the rows above and below. They now fall back through shorter forms (Q4 02:34 to 02:34 to Q4) the same way the odds row sheds its label.
versions.changelog: Corrects a log line that claimed no favourite teams were configured when they were: the schedule view is used whenever show_favorite_teams_only is off, not only when favourites are absent. It now names the teams and the setting to change.

They now fall back through shorter forms (Q4 02:34 to 02:34 to Q4) the same way the odds row sheds its label.
versions.changelog: Readability follow-up in the font loader; no behaviour change.

A font size that merely echoes the schema default is treated as unchosen and snapped; a size you actually chose is left alone.

versions.changelog: Scroll/Vegas cards: the centre gap is now measured from the score actually loaded and the card is sized to fit two full-height logos plus that gap, so the score no longer renders on top of the team logos on tall cards. Test-only follow-up: the small-panel test calls the real sizing methods unbound rather than patching them onto a stub, which cleared a static-analysis false positive.

versions.notes: Keep the over/under on screen, and shrink the odds rather than blur them. The detail font no longer grows with panel height: the sizes that produced (6px, then 10px) both sit off the 4x6 face grid of 7px, so the glyphs were anti-aliased, and the larger one lost its space contest against the centre status and was dropped entirely. One crisp 7px step now applies at every height. The budget also measures what the card actually centres instead of the widest string any card could hold, and the label sheds its prefix before it sheds the number (O/U: 45.5 to 45.5), with a 3px gutter so a label that just fits does not end on the pixel the status starts on. The over/under now renders on live, final and upcoming cards at both 32 and 64 tall; previously it was missing from every 64-tall card.

Render the scroll-card fonts on their pixel grid. PressStart2P and 4x6-font are pixel-art faces that rasterise cleanly only at whole multiples of 8 and 7; every other size is anti-aliased, and on an LED matrix a part-lit pixel is a dim lamp rather than a soft edge. Score, status and rank sat off-grid at 10/6/10, and on 64-tall panels the odds were scaled to 10px where 65% of the lit pixels were partial -- the over/under and spread came out visibly broken. Defaults now snap to the grid and the detail font scales in whole grid steps (14px at 64 tall, 21 at 96, 28 at 128). A 32-tall panel deliberately keeps its 6px detail font: the next crisp size is 7px, at which the over/under no longer fits and is dropped entirely.

Request odds only for the games that will be shown. The upcoming-games loop fetched odds for every game it collected and the caller then kept upcoming_games_to_show of them (10 by default). The loop's own comment claimed odds were fetched only for games that would be displayed, but the filter it referred to applies only when show_favorite_teams_only is set AND favourite teams are configured, and neither is the default -- so in the usual case nothing narrowed it. A live rig running college football logged 946 upcoming games in one cycle and displayed 1 of them, having made 946 separate ESPN odds requests to do it, from a Pi that is also driving the panel. The odds cache only absorbs repeats of the same event, so a wide schedule never benefited from it. Nothing about what reaches the screen changes.

Turn the favorite-teams field into a checkbox picker. It was a free-text array with only a description telling you to use 2-3 letter codes and nothing validating what you typed, so a wrong or stale code saved cleanly and then matched nothing -- an empty screen with no error anywhere. The roster is now an enum with display names, rendered as the same checkbox-group the odds ticker already uses, and scripts/check_team_pickers.py keeps it in step with ESPN. Existing configurations are unaffected: the codes were already ESPN's, so anything valid today stays valid. Applies to NFL; the college leagues keep the text field, since a checkbox grid of several hundred teams is worse than typing. Codes ESPN no longer uses cannot be offered by a picker, so if one is already saved the config will not save until it is replaced: JAC (Jaguars), LA (Rams), OAK (Raiders (pre-2020)), SD (Chargers (pre-2017)), STL (Rams (pre-2016)), TAM (Buccaneers), WAS (Commanders). The web UI reports which value it rejected.

Make the schedule fetch window configurable. How far back and forward games are fetched was hard-coded at 14 days back and 7 forward. Days is the wrong unit for a league that plays weekly -- a whole matchweek can fall just past a short horizon and never reach the board -- so both are now advanced settings, bounded 1-60 days, with a stray or non-numeric value falling back to the default rather than raising. Defaults keep today's behaviour.
versions.changes: Back off the live-game poll while a league has nothing on, and let both the idle interval and its ceiling be configured. Saves API calls out of season and between games without delaying an in-progress game, which still resets the interval on the first fetch that finds one.

The authoritative fetch now uses the configured window too, the Recent cutoff follows it instead of a fixed 21 days, and the fields render in the web UI for every plugin.

Load the bundled fonts without depending on the process working directory. Every font this scoreboard draws with ships in the LEDMatrix core and was named relative to the cwd, which resolves only under the packaged systemd unit, whose WorkingDirectory is the install root. Anywhere else -- the plugin safety harness, a manual run from a home directory, a unit file written without WorkingDirectory -- the load raised, the caller's fallback caught it, and the scoreboard rendered in PIL's default face at the wrong metrics instead of the pixel font its layout was built around. Every direct load now goes through a resolver that tries the path as given, then the core install root, then returns the original so existing fallbacks are untouched; a configured absolute path still passes through unchanged.

Honour the configured live-game dwell instead of the data refresh rate. The rotation lived in update(), which runs on live_update_interval -- 30s by default -- so a game could only be advanced at that cadence and every configured duration was quantised to it. Measured on a live rig with four NFL games: live_game_duration=45 and non_favorite_live_game_duration=10 both produced a flat 30s rotation, and only changing live_update_interval changed anything. It is driven from display() now, so a dwell shorter than the refresh interval is reachable and a longer one is not cut short.

Match favorites against this plugin's real live-data shape. The first cut looked for an attribute holding live_games beside favorite_teams, which is true of five scoreboards and quietly false for four: cricket keeps live_matches, nrl and afl hold their managers in a dict rather than as attributes, and ufc has favorite_fighters and fighter names. Those four reported every live game as non-favorite. A celebrating game is searched too, since the live manager snapshots it out of live_games while the celebration is on screen.

Ask for more turns in the Vegas ticker while a game is live, and more again when a favorite team is playing. Only takes effect with the core's display.vegas_scroll.live_in_ticker set, which keeps the marquee running instead of handing the display to a full-screen scoreboard. The core grants a live plugin live_weight on its own; this reports the favorite case, which the core cannot see -- it knows a game is live but not whose.

Fix blurry score digits on the LED matrix: the outline-drawing helper used PIL's default anti-aliased text rendering, which blends pixel-font (PressStart2P) glyph edges into dim partial-lit pixels on a 1:1 matrix, muddying numbers (a "6" could read as a "G"). Text now draws in 1-bit font mode so every glyph -- scores, clocks, team names, status text -- renders crisp with no anti-aliasing.

Apply the betting-odds layout offsets the config schema already advertised. customization.layout.odds declares x_offset and y_offset, so the web UI offered both, but the renderer drew the spread and over/under at a fixed 0,0 and never read them -- a control that visibly did nothing, which reads as the position being unfixable.

Make the live screen renderable offline, so it is covered before the season rather than during it. Live was the one screen the safety harness never rendered, and two latent bugs are why: _adapt_config_for_manager() never passed test_mode into the per-manager config, so SportsLive.test_mode could not be set at all and the fully seeded simulated game in NFLLiveManager.__init__ was unreachable; and SportsLive.update() fetched unconditionally, so even with the flag set the seeded game was overwritten on the first tick -- _test_mode_update() was defined and never called. Both are fixed, the second by porting the short-circuit baseball-scoreboard already uses. The harness now renders nfl_live at every panel size (16 renders to 24, none blank). No behaviour change for real users: test_mode defaults to False on both paths, so live fetches exactly as before.

Scroll and Vegas cards: never show 0-0 before a game starts, add a centre gap so the score or VS is not drawn on top of the team logos, and write upcoming dates as "Sep 19". A new scroll_card config block sets what fills the middle of an upcoming card (VS, or the date and time stacked), the date format (abbrev/numeric) and the centre gap in pixels. gap_between_games is now honoured in Vegas mode, which stitches its own items and previously ignored it, and its code default moves from 24 to 48 to match the config schema. The date is positioned from its measured height rather than a fixed offset, which stops "Sep 19" running past the bottom of the card in the plugins whose detail font is 10px. These settings only affect the cards built for scroll and Vegas modes; the full-screen scoreboard is drawn by a separate code path and is unchanged. The adaptive layout path (layout_mode: adaptive) gets the same treatment: it drew the score unconditionally and used the raw numeric date, so it needed fixing separately from the classic path. Adaptive golden images regenerated for recent and upcoming; the live goldens are pixel-identical and unchanged. Adds a fuller set of scroll_card settings: vs_text (VS, @, at, ...), date_format now covering abbrev/numeric/day_first/numeric_day_first/weekday, time_format 12h or 24h, show_date, show_time, swap_date_time, upcoming_center gains a 'none' option, and center_gap_ratio/min/max for the automatic gap. Each customization text element gains text_color, and the customization.layout X/Y offsets are now honoured by the scroll/Vegas card -- the schema advertised them but only the full-screen scoreboard read them before. The away team is drawn on the left and the home team on the right, so "at" and "@" read correctly as "away at home".

Add customization.favorite_result_colors: an optional setting that colors a recent game's final score green when your favorite team won and red when it lost. Aimed at scroll and Vegas modes, where the same matchup can go past several times and the logos alone do not say who won. Off by default; games without exactly one favorite team keep the normal score color.

Fix ESPN 403s. Around 2026-08-04 ESPN's site.api began rejecting both browser-style and bare custom User-Agent strings, which returned 403 Forbidden for every request this plugin made. Requests now send an identifying agent with the project URL, which ESPN accepts. No behaviour change beyond the header.

Test-only: the scroll display is now constructed on both the core and fallback paths, and its separator icons compared between them. The previous checks verified that methods existed and that their globals resolved, which could not see a constant read off self -- the miss that broke scroll mode in three sibling plugins.

Scroll display now uses the core's shared sports-scroll orchestration (LEDMatrix 3.2.0) when available, falling back to the bundled implementation on older cores. No behaviour change: all 16 harness renders are byte-for-byte identical.
Correct the NCAA football example team codes in the favorite-teams help text: Alabama is ALA in ESPN's data, not BAMA. Copying the old example matched no team and showed nothing.

Fix event start times rendering in UTC. The plugin looked for the LEDMatrix global timezone only on cache_manager.config_manager; on cores that expose config_manager via the plugin manager instead, that lookup found nothing and every start time was drawn in UTC even though the clock plugin was correct on the same device. Timezone resolution now checks the plugin override, then both config managers, then the host system zone, before falling back to UTC. Adds a documented timezone setting under Advanced Settings -- previously the key was not in the config schema, so hand-editing it had no effect. Also stops the plugin writing a resolved timezone back into the saved config, which could persist a stale "UTC" override.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.

Fix adaptive mode (beta): (1) two ladder rungs (press_start@10/12px, 5by7.regular at any size) rendered visibly antialiased/blurry text -- both dropped, 4x6-font corrected from 6px to 7px (its actual crisp size); (2) score/status/detail text was sized to maximize within its own region, which on large panels let the score balloon large enough to visually overlap the team logos -- now sized proportionally to the panel scale (matching classic's fixed-size look, just crisper and bigger) via the new core fit_text_proportional().

Adaptive layout (beta, opt-in): set layout_mode: "adaptive" to scale fonts/logos/regions to any panel size. Default stays "classic" — rendering is unchanged unless you opt in; switch back to classic in config to revert without reinstalling. Adaptive mode also applies customization.layout x/y offsets in scroll mode (classic scroll never did). User-configured fonts win over adaptive sizing.

versions.changes: Add non_favorite_live_game_duration per league: give live games without a favorite team a shorter on-screen turn than your favorites. Applies only when favorite teams are set and show_favorite_teams_only is off; defaults to 0 (off) for unchanged behavior.

Apply config changes live via on_config_change (favorite teams, league enable/disable, durations, live priority, display modes); rebuilds the league managers, registry, scroll manager and rotation so edits take effect without a display restart.

Add exclude_teams (hide specific teams from live rotation and recent/final scores - spoiler protection) and filtering.favorite_live_boost (tune how much more often your favorite's live game appears in rotation vs other live games) per league.

Add goal/win celebration takeover: a full-screen flash when a favorite team scores (touchdown, field goal, safety) or wins a live game, with configurable celebration_enabled, celebration_duration, and celebrate_opponent_scores per league.
